recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further core source change is needed for FHIR-38869; separate follow-up tracker audits can stand independently, and FHIR-40631 is already represented on the combined branch.
issue_request: FHIR-38869 was a Published, Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request for R5 asking to define RequestOrchestration behavior around documenting clinician choices, tracing resulting requests/events back to the source orchestration, preserving intent=option, completion, groupIdentifier, and when to use the available compound-request patterns.
initial_application: The seed was applied through multiple prior paths. Commit b807023fb39ba3e3d0656b042a9ca031ed814ed4 added groupIdentifier vs RequestOrchestration guidance to the Request logical model notes. Follow-up FHIR-40635 was applied by commit 5531aba65e12d242f2742b1966285cb698f7152e, adding RequestOrchestration notes for choices, option intent, and completion. The basedOn tracking question was split into follow-up issues: FHIR-40631 for OO resources, FHIR-40633 for MedicationRequest, FHIR-40634 for Appointment/Encounter, and FHIR-40632 as a Public Health no-change decision.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps the Request logical model and RequestOrchestration resource in current build scope. Current RequestOrchestration notes include the FHIR-40635 guidance; current Request notes distinguish shared groupIdentifier, basedOn chains, and RequestOrchestration. Current basedOn source permits RequestOrchestration where the accepted follow-ups called for it, with DeviceRequest covered by Reference(Resource) as documented in the existing FHIR-40631 combined-branch audit commit. Confluence minutes for 2022-12-19 confirm the FHIR Workflow Persuasive with Modification disposition, and targeted Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community guidance.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current specification already conveys the approved FHIR-38869 behavior, so additional wording would be redundant rather than a semantic correction.
